explanation: This pole is a copy/duplication detector: it fires when the tokens at the current position repeat a span that already occurred earlier in the same document, and its strength scales with how many prior copies of that span exist (the Java line 'dag.getParentSet(H).addParent(A);' scores 6.0 where it first occurs, 17.0 on its second copy and 19.3 on its third; a repeated prose sentence goes 4.5 -> 9.0 -> 12.0). It is therefore strongest inside serialised, template-shaped passages - repeated code statements and loops, restated formulas, incrementing table rows, licence-header and import blocks, LaTeX macro runs, coordinate and byte lists - and it is not driven by token identity, position, language or source: the same '(' in the same syntactic slot drops from 17.0 to 10.7 when the preceding line is not a copy of its line, while slot-substituted repeats and repeated prose still fire.
